mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen consistently over the past four weeks (from -30.1% to -18.6%), indicating a sustained recovery trend. This momentum will continue linearly over the next four weeks, producing a further increase in retail-and-recreation mobility.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 11.5 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or declines by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -0.4% to +5.1%) signals normalization of essential shopping patterns. Consumers bundling grocery trips with retail-and-recreation visits will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks as this behavioral coupling strengthens.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +3% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 5.5 percentage points in two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above +3%, or GROCERY_PHARM declines below +2%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains depressed (-12.0%) but has improved 10.1 points over four weeks. When WORKPLACES recovery combines with TRANSIT station usage recovery (both trending upward), commuter-driven retail footfall will increase. The interaction of workplace and transit normalization drives RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 10.1 points over four weeks
fact:TRANSIT improved 9.9 points over four weeks
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT reverses by more than 5 percentage points in any single week, or RETAIL_REC declines despite both proxies improving.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July in London marks peak summer holiday season. PARKS mobility has declined sharply (from -14.7% to -21.7%), indicating outdoor recreation is being displaced or constrained. This suppression of parks activity will redirect leisure spending toward indoor retail-and-recreation venues over the next week, producing a sharp increase.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 8.3 percentage points in one week (t-1w to t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following the PARKS decline, or PARKS recovers sharply while RETAIL_REC remains flat.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated (16.0%) but declining slowly. When RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 15%, it signals policy restrictions are tightening or behavioral caution is increasing. Under tightening conditions, RETAIL_REC will decline as consumers reduce non-essential trips over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15% in any week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has declined from 20.0% to 16.0% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL falling below 15%, or RESIDENTIAL remains above 15% throughout the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station usage (-25.1%) and WORKPLACES usage (-12.0%) remain substantially depressed, indicating weak commuting patterns. This persistent suppression of work-commute activity will constrain retail footfall during peak shopping hours over the next two weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC below baseline.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -20% and WORKPLACES below -10% simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points in the next two weeks, or either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES recovers by more than 8 percentage points in a single week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near +5%, indicating essential shopping is normalized. When essential shopping stabilizes at this level, discretionary retail-and-recreation spending will remain constrained because consumers are not yet confident enough to increase non-essential trips. RETAIL_REC will stagnate or decline slightly over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM plateaus between +3% and +7% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at +5.1% in most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM rises above +10% signaling broader confidence recovery.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined sharply to -21.7%, TRANSIT remains depressed at -25.1%, and WORKPLACES at -12.0%. This multi-domain suppression indicates a coordinated reduction in outdoor and commute-based activities. When three or more mobility domains decline simultaneously, RETAIL_REC will decline over the next week as overall activity levels contract.
candidate_trigger: PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES all decline week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:all three series declined from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in the next week despite all three proxies declining, or only one of the three proxies declines while the others recover.
